learningObjective: Reason about occupancy: it is the minimum over registers, SMEM, threads/SM, and blocks/SM limits.

canonicalClaims.claim: GPU occupancy per SM is the minimum of resource limits: (i) registers per SM / (regs-per-thread * threads-per-block), (ii) SMEM per SM / SMEM-per-block, (iii) threads per SM / threads-per-block, (iv) blocks-per-SM cap. On A100 with regs=96, threads=256, SMEM=32 KB, register cap dominates at 2 blocks/SM.
conditions: A100 sm_80 hardware limits; single kernel resident.
nonImplications: Does not imply higher occupancy is always better.
Does not imply nvcc auto-spills registers to raise occupancy.

misconceptions.claim: SMEM is always the binding limiter.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Registers, threads/SM, or block count can dominate depending on kernel.

misconceptions.claim: nvcc automatically spills registers to global memory to raise occupancy.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Register limits are set by user (`-maxrregcount`, `__launch_bounds__`); nvcc does not silently spill for occupancy.
Registers and SMEM are equally binding factors.

misconceptions.claim: 100% occupancy is always the optimization target.
misconceptions.whyWrong: High occupancy can force smaller tiles that hurt arithmetic intensity.

implementationFacts: A100 sm_80: 65536 regs/SM, 164 KB SMEM/SM (dynamic carveout), 2048 threads/SM, 32 blocks/SM cap.
